question: Fed Rate Hike by September 2026 Meeting?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between December 16, 2025 and the completion of the listed Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting (inclusive of any rate hike announced as a result of the listed meeting). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If the listed meeting does not take place within 7 calendar days (ET) of its scheduled end date, 11:59 PM ET, and no qualifying rate hike has been announced, this market will resolve to "No".

Emergency rate hikes will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
research:
I have enough material and am writing up the brief now. Several search results included material published after 2026-08-26. I left all of it out as instructed. Only items dated on or before 2026-08-26 are used.

## 1. Resolution source
- I tried to fetch the Fed's open market page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm) and the July statement. Both requests were refused by the proxy, so I could not read the primary source directly.
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC kept the target range at **3.50%-3.75%**, so the upper bound is 3.75%. That range has been in place since the December 2025 cut. [Fed press release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. I found no rate hike, including any emergency move, between 2025-12-16 and 2026-08-26. The January, March, April/May, June and July 2026 meetings all ended without one. The September 15-16 FOMC meeting decides the outcome.
- 2026-07-29: The hold passed 9-3. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented, all in favour of a 25 bp **hike**. That is the largest dissent since September 2016. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Late August 2026: The Jackson Hole symposium is scheduled for the last week of August. Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks there are widely seen as a key signal.
- 2026-08-19: The July minutes said "Many participants assessed that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/fed-minutes-july-2026-officials-saw-need-for-rate-hike-if-inflation-doesnt-cool.html), [Fed minutes](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20260729.htm)
- 2026-08-12/13: July CPI rose 0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, down from 3.5% in June. Core CPI rose 0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y, down from 2.6%. These figures come from secondary reports, not BLS directly, and they disagree on whether the release was August 12 or 13. Reports say traders cut the odds of a September hike afterwards. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/blog/us-cpi-rises-0-1-in-july-2026-as-expected-core-inflation-eases-to-2-5), [InsiderFinance](https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/july-cpi-2026-eases-while-core-stays-sticky)
- 2026-07-29: Warsh stressed the 2% target. A BMO strategist expected rates to stay on hold at least until September, once the July and August CPI reports are in. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- July 2026: June CPI slowed to 3.5% y/y, which pushed back expectations of a hike. [SMM](https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104006513-инфляция-в-сша-в-июне-замедлилась-до-35-отодвигая-ожидания-повышения-ставки-фрс)

## 4. Base rates
- The Fed has not raised rates since July 2023. The cycle since then has been cuts, followed by holds through 2026.
- Three dissents in favour of a hike is unusual. The last time it happened, in September 2016, the Fed did not hike at the next meeting (November 2016) and moved in December 2016. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- The Fed rarely hikes when futures price the move below about 50% a few weeks ahead. Usually it signals the move first and pricing ends up near 90% or more by meeting day.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Before the July meeting, markets gave roughly a one-in-three chance of a hike later in 2026. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- 2026-08-15: The Kalshi September "hike" contract was reportedly around 26¢. This comes from a secondary summary. [PredictionMarketsPicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- One report from around the CPI release said futures priced about a 55% chance of a September hold, which implies roughly 45% for a hike. The exact date is unclear. [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/fed-rate-hike-july-cpi-report/)
- Another report put Polymarket at 53% for a September hike against 32% in futures. I could not confirm its date. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/polymarket-prices-53-odds-of-fed-rate-hike-in-september-2026-vs-32-in-futures)
- Taken together, sources from mid-to-late August put September hike odds at roughly 25-50%, and they disagree with each other. Check the live market before relying on any one number. [Polymarket market](https://polymarket.com/event/fed-decision-in-september-762)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late August: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.
- About August 28: July PCE inflation.
- About September 4: the August jobs report.
- About September 10-11: August CPI. BMO flagged this report as decisive.
- The pre-meeting blackout starts around September 5. After that, Fed officials won't give new guidance.
- September 15-16: the FOMC decision, with the statement at 2:00 pm ET on September 16, plus the SEP and dot plot.

  - July CPI, released 2026-08-12/13, was soft: 0.1% m/m headline, with core easing to 2.5% y/y. Inflation is declining, so the conditional in the minutes is weakening.
  - Traders cut hike odds after the release, and Kalshi was around 26% on 2026-08-15.
  - Chair Warsh is unlikely to hike when core is near 2.5% and falling.
  - The Fed usually signals hikes in advance, and no clear signal has come yet.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: Jackson Hole is balanced, PCE and August CPI are moderate, and the Fed holds in September with hawkish dissents, perhaps keeping a hike in the dots for later.
- Yes: Warsh sounds hawkish at Jackson Hole, August CPI comes in hot at 0.4% or more with core picking up, and the committee hikes 25 bp to get ahead of expectations.

(f) **Adjustment.** I start at about 15%. The hawkish dissents and minutes push it up. The soft July CPI, falling core, and a chair unlikely to lead a surprise hike pull it back down. Market readings range widely, from 26% to roughly 45%. The most specific dated figure is Kalshi at about 26% after the CPI, and I anchor near it. I shade slightly lower because core disinflation undercuts the hawks' stated condition, and a non-telegraphed hike is historically rare.

Probability: 20%

I move up toward the market because three dissents and the hawkish minutes show a real constituency for a hike. Several upcoming data releases can still change the picture, and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech is unpriced.

**(f) From base rate to forecast**
I start from a 10% base rate and move up toward the market anchor. Three hawkish dissents and the conditional tightening language in the minutes are real evidence that a hike is live. I treat Kalshi at about 26% as the best liquid anchor, since it is dated after the CPI release and matches this resolution. The 45-53% figures are undated or unclear and seem to predate the softer CPI, so I give them less weight. I go slightly below the anchor for two reasons the market may underweight: core at 2.5% largely fails the "if inflation does not decline" trigger in the minutes, and a Warsh-led committee is unlikely to hike against easing core without a clear signal. No such signal had appeared by August 26. Data still to come (PCE, jobs, August CPI) keeps meaningful upside.

Probability: 20%
